From: John H.B. White, LEICESTER

There are two questions from a
correspondent which I cannot
answer.

1) Can the VTX 5000 modem be
used with the Continental
MINITEL system (V23, same format
as our PRESTEL) and with the
same software?

2) The VTX  Eprom (in a socket)
contains the MICRONET-oriented
software but  as MICRONET no
longer exists, is it possible to
remove it, leaving all other
functions intact?

Best wishes and thanks for
OUTLET.
        John H.B. White


To John White from Brian Gaff

The Minitel system does not use
the same kind of viewdata as we
do. There was a program written
for the VTX that was supposed to
access the service. However, I
tested this for Micronet and
found it to be almost unusable!
Could I ask WHY you want
Minitel? Its an expensive system
to access.

The ROM would need to be dis-
abled before removal. Just cut
the print on the ROMCS line on
the edge connector. Why remove
it though?To use other software,
you simply exit the program. If
you use a +2, then POKE 23611,23
will get you into 128K mode with
the modem attached anyway.

Although the VTX ROM software
SAYS its a Micronet terminal,
this is just because Micronet
money paid for it. It is
perfectly capable of accessing
any UK Viewdata system. I have
used it on TAS, TAO, TSV, and
Speedlink with no problems. Here
are a few tips.


To use on a system where you do
not know the login requirements,
go to the main menu, BREAK, then
RUN. This will allow you to go
straight into terminal mode
without having screwed up
characters. You then simply go
on line and into terminal mode,
rather than using the log on
option.

If the line drops while logging
on, try going on line during a
later tone. This is because many
modems scan for baud rates that
were never used when the VTX was
designed, and so it cannot hear
the tones, and drops the line.

For the majority of BBs in the
world now, scrolling software is
needed. My PD Tape 1 has some of
this [see OUTBOARD] and all for
`1... I must be mad! Note also
that some boards use US made
modems that do not support V23
at all, so you cannot get on.

I am currently wading through a
huge list of UK BBs and making a
list of any you can get on with
the VTX. I will publish it when
I have enough to warrant it. BG

From: Brian Gaff, CHESSINGTON

A few comments, as ever from me
on last month's letters!

Sector errors:
Now I have no proof of this, but
here are my thoughts on why
Unidos can cope. The majority of
sector errors seem to be
corruption in the sector
preamble. This is the bit that
contains the sector number, and
a checksum. Now, if GDOS rejects
this sector outright if the
checksum is wrong, and Unidos
does not, you would retrieve
most of the data from it. Unidos
would of course correct the
checksum when it formatted the
track, and copied the data back.

Capacitor measurement by
computer eh? This sounds like a
classic case of re-inventing the
wheel!

As the circuit seems to be based
on an oscillator, I would guess
the measurement would be based
on the mark-space ratio
generated with differing values
of capacitor. Personally, I
would use the tried and tested
bridge system, as small hand
held units are around at cheap
prices.

The famous +3 printer bug is on
every machine with a V4.0 ROM.
The reason everyone does not
suffer is that most printers are
tolerant of it!

Speaking from memory, I recall
Cliff of Amstrad telling me that
when the +3 pages to get at its
printer driver, it 'wobbles' the
voltage on the Strobe line on
the printer port. Some printers
take exception to this, and will
not print afterwards. Quite how
the Pokes work I am not sure.

SAMCO problem:
I had a long chat with Alan
Miles recently,and he's aware of
the poor service. There are
several reasons for this. First-
ly, SAMCO was under financed,
and simply didn't have the staff
to cope. Also, there have been
problems due to the unavailabil-
ity of disc drives from Citizen,
which has made repairs very
slow. OK, that's the bad news.

The good news is that it's
almost certain that a company
has been found to invest in the
project. This will mean that
extra staff can be hired, and
this in turn should ease the
work load on the existing three
staff members - yes, just three!

There will be a few weeks when
Samco will be out of reach, but
on return, things should
improve. This is the message,
and I guess only time will tell
if it will work. I guess we just
'hang on in there'!

           Brian Gaff

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

Dear Brian and Ron,

From: Chris Oliver, STAFFS.

Dear Ron and Brian,

What an absolutely stunning
sound/graphics demo in Issue 58!
[SONG DEMO] So good in fact,
that after playing with it for
about an hour, I just had to sit
down and work out what effect
each of the control keys had.

There is in fact an index/menu
on two pages selected by "EDIT"
(Page 1) and "CAPS-LOCK" (Page
2); use "ENTER" to return to the
demo. Each menu page also
includes an active three-channel
sound level indicator. There is
a screen SAVE option reached by
SYMBOL-SHIFT and SPACE together.

It saves the SCREEN$ with the
name "Super line", but only to
tape.

Unfortunately, if you're not
very fluent (or like me, totally
ignorant) in Slavonic languages,
the menus are not a great help.
By a combination of guesswork
and trial and error, I
discovered the following:-
MUSIC CONTROLS:
1) Any letter key  with CAPS ON
to select each of 26 melodies.

2) DELETE selects  the next
tune.

3) GRAPHIC key switches sound
off (Use 1 or 2 above to get it
back again)

4).TRUE VIDEO & INVERSE VIDEO
are fast-forward and slow-
forward whilst held down
(similar to a tape deck).

GRAPHICS CONTROLS: (each gives
an option to use a number key 0
to 9, where 1 is the slowest or
least complex, and 0 is at the
other end of the scale above 9):

"f" = select graphic sequence.
"d" = ditto
"r" = speed of image motion.
"x" = speed of direction change.
"z" = speed of colour change
"n" = speed of horizontal motion
"m" = speed of vertical motion.
"s" = horizontal symmetry (9 is
      symmetrical about centre).
"a" = vertical symmetry.

"u" = select pattern type.
"c" = length of trail (effective
      pattern density)
"i" = image colour (ink);
(0-7  give fixed colour; 8-9 =
      changing.)
"p" = background colour (paper)
"q" = clear trail of existing
      image.
"j" = subtle change to
      horizontal(can't determine
      what!)
"k" = ditto to vertical (?)
"h" = is an option which seems
      to have very little effect
      on anything!
UP/DOWN ARROWS change immediate
direction of image motion.
"BREAK" resets to the start of
the Preset graphics demo
sequence.

Pressing any two keys together
(almost any) produces a prompt
that index pages are obtainable
from "EDIT " or "CAPS-LOCK".

If I misinterpreted any of the
above, I humbly apologise to the
writers and interested to learn
the correct information.

Congratulations to Ron and Brian
and all the contributors to OUT-
LET for maintaining such variety
and high standard that make it
the Greatest disc magazine.
            Cheers,
              Chris

P.S. Is it possible on +D to
OPEN a stream to anything other
than a file? The +D manual is
very sparse on details!

Brian Cavers to Chris Oliver

Yes,the SONG DEMO in Issue 58 is
excellent! Thanks for all the

simply tried a few keys and had

No, I don't think you can OPEN a

OPENTYPE file on the +D. Perhaps
another reader can prove me
wrong?
                        - Brian

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

Dear Brian and Ron,

Have you ever tried:

CAT 1, "x" (or anything else in
the quotes) on a +D
or:
DIR 1, "x" on the SAM

... interesting?!

Now to a problem:
Imagine you have a BASIC program
in which you have  declared 26
numeric variables (A to Z) and
26 string variables (A  to Z).
Can you, or any reader, suggest
how any variable can be pointed
out in response to a prompt such

as "Which variable do you want
to examine?" so that you can
find out what value you gave to
(say) K or N$, without resorting
to machine code. I can think of
only one inelegant way; which
I'll not reveal just yet.

Perhaps you, or one of your
readers, can provide an elegant
solution. The numeric part is
easyish, but the string part
isn't - or have I overlooked
something really obvious?
Solutions to be entirely in
BASIC, on the Spectrum.

This could be a good programming
puzzle?

             Regards,  - Malcolm

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Goodman


Here's one method (it is assumed
the variables have already been
declared)...

10 INPUT "VARIABLE? ";V$

20 IF V$(LEN V$)="$" THEN
   PRINT VAL$ V$: GO TO 10

30 PRINT VAL V$: GO TO 10

This is one of those rare times
that VAL$ can be used! The above
could use some error-trapping of
course.
                        - Brian

From: Phil Parnell,

Dear Ron,

I am writing with a few enquir-
ies that you or your readers may
be able to help me with. First
of all are there bits of the Rom
Index missing as they are numb-
ered and lettered out of seq-
uence. That is to say the files

You also have a file CA. Should

I intend to print it out on
continuous paper and would like
to have each file run on in
order to make one fully cont-
inuous text, each file following
in order. Following is the list
of textfiles that have so far
appeared on the +3 version.
I0, I1, A1-5, B1-3, C1-4, C6-C9,
CA, E2-E6, F1-F5, G1, G2, I1
(again),I2-I4, K1-4, L1-L5
Are there any missing?

I have written previously and in
one of your replies you
mentioned a utility you possess,
I think it was called
"BONABANNER". You did say that
you may include it in OUTLET but
as yet it has not appeared.
Would you consider doing so?

I'd like to create textfiles
such as yours and would
appreciate any help you could
give me to enable me to do so.
What format are your textfiles
in? What would I have to do to a
Tasword +3 (or any Tasword vers-
ion)textfile to load it into
OUTLET so I can use Tabloid? Are
they compressed,and if so how is
it done?You see,you have made me
jealous. Your textfiles look so
neat and polished, especially
when they are printed out using
the 'Tabloid' option.

The utility above creates the
headlines in your textfiles such
as "OUTCLASS", "OUTLETTERS" etc.
Any information would be greatly
appreciated.

I intend to write to the creator
of 'Tabloid' to ask if he would
write me a "stand alone" version
of this utility as paper is so
expensive it would save me a
packet! So, if you could help
with BONABANNER and textfile
info and Mike can help with
Tabloid I would possess a tool
of some note!!

The OUTLET letters index I sent
in has saved me a great deal of
time looking for information and
it would be a pity if it could
not be converted in some form so
as to help others. I intend to
keep it up to date and, if you
wish, I will keep sending you
updates in the original format
for your own use.

How do you install Autochars +
in a program of your own? I
haven't got the original Issue
as it on Issue 17 and I detest
tapes but I have noticed it in
the listings on the +3 versions.
Could I extract it and insert it
into my loading menu's? I can
assure you they are not for sale
or anything, and are for my own
personal use.

I use the DMS utility from
Kobrahsoft a lot and they have
some autoload menu's and it
would look excellent on this. I
prefer a chunkier font myself
and this does the trick.

I still cannot use the "BLAST
IT" to print out on the +3 as it

stops with the error report "C
Nonsense in Basic 2620:1" every
time you try to set the print
option from the menu.I am press-
ing the "3" key to select +3
when the error occurs. I use
Tasword 2 to print it out and
mention it only as you say you
have fixed it. I notice that in
this months (June) Outletters Mr
G Yeardley has the same problem.
Perhaps it is a +3 bug like the
screen garbling in the same
utility?

I notice you had been in touch
with Propac PD, or rather Brian
had. I can assure you that I
waited a lot longer than one
month and have the cheque stubs
to prove it!

However, I did not realise it
was a one man band and can see
how it would have slowed him
down somewhat. As he would not
get in touch or answer my myriad
of requests, I had no idea.

Anyway, enough of the sour
grapes! I recently got in touch
with the "UNITED AMSTRAD USER
GROUP" with the intention of
procuring some very cheap CF2's
he was selling. These were ex
software house disks but were in
excellent condition and have
proven very reliable.

Anyway the chairman of this
group was kind enough to send me
a PD list. It was quite a large
list but was only a shortened

version of the main, rather
substantial list. The large
majority ran under AMSDOS but,
there was a huge amount of
utilities that ran on CP/M. He
said that most of this was
already on 3" disk but a small
amount was on 3 1/2" media, but
you only needed a suitable 3
1/2" drive to access this. As I
say, they cater mostly for
Amstrad CPC's but they had some
excellent utilities. If anyone
would like more details then the
address to write to is:-
THE CHAIRMAN, UPLANDS CRESCENT,
FAREHAM, HANTS, P016 7JY.

Of course you must have the CP/M
/ Mallard basic system installed
to access this software!

I noticed that someone had been
having problems with the
Spectrum software hire club. I
feel that I must mention that I
have been a member of this club
for some time now and have never
had cause for complaint.
This club has been recently
taken over and she says the list
was in a right state and has
only just managed to get it into
order and has even gone through
them and written on if they are
not compatible with certain
types of Spectrum - some feat,as
she has thousands of titles. The
problem should not now occur.
She has also answered every one
of my queries and so this leads
me to the conclusion that she
never received the letters.

This all goes to prove that
while one person (me!) may
experience problems, another may
have none whatsoever. Ah well,
such is life!

         All the best,

              Phil.

Brian Cavers to Phillip Parnell

Sorry, yes, I have missed ROM
INDEX files cb, cc, cd, d1 to d7
and e1. I have tried to keep a
very careful check but each
version is out of step because
they have varying space and my
conversion routines are so very
complex that one month I jumped
from the +3 sequence to the tape
sequence. It doesn't help having
to work 12, 14 or 16 hours a day
- especially at the crucial end-
of-month phase. I shall have to
put the missing ones in starting
from this month.

c5 is on Side A of Issue 52. I
think(I hope) I put a message in
somewhere.

The alphabetical suffixes come
AFTER the numeral suffixes as in
hexadecimal notation e.g....

      ...c8, c9, ca, cb...

Again, apologies for not putting
BONABANNER into OUTLET. I am
completely overwhelmed with the
workload and shall have to stop
making promises and start saying
"NO!". It would need a lot of
work to prepare,edit and convert
to the +3 (if indeed, possible
at all!). Witness the trouble
with BLAST IT! Add to that, the
fact that I reckon BONABANNER is
one of the best programs I have
ever written. I think it is
brilliant and have used it VERY
extensively for years. YET, I do


not think I remember a single
instance of anyone else sending
in a program with a header made
by BONABANNER - suggesting that
it would not be a popular choice
in OUTLET(especially as it would
take up a lot of room).

As far as using it create text
files like OUTLET text files,
again, our utilities extend to
many different files which
involve mass-compression of
multiple files and it would be a
big job to prepare them for
OUTLET. What you really want is
a multi-column printout from
normal Tasword files I think
although they would not have
graphic headers. Certainly, Mike
Haine is the expert and may be
able to help you.

Sorry to be so negative - nobody
is more willing to help than I
but I have to be realistic and
consider what is practical in
order to keep OUTLET going and
just do essential work.

Possibly what you really want is
a desk top publisher such as the
one from PCG which is much more
flexible.

To install AUTOCHARS you just
MERGE it in and use GO SUB 9994.
Naturally, you will have to
delete all the other lines first
if you are extracting it from
another program so pick a short
one or use a block line deletor.
Also extract line 9900 which can
stop a 128K list being scrambled
by AUTOCHARS.

I found the bug in BLAST IT! I
cannot understand this. I was
sure I'd tested the +3 printout
but I don't see how I could have
since this bug has been present
all along! BLAST IT! should be
alright from this month.

                        Brian

      WORTHING,

### Ответ для John White от Brian Gaff

Система Minitel использует не такой вид viewdata, как у нас. Для VTX была написана программа, которая якобы позволяла получить доступ к этой службе. Однако я тестировал ее для Micronet и нашел практически непригодной для использования! Могу я спросить, ЗАЧЕМ вам Minitel? Доступ к этой системе стоит очень дорого.

Перед извлечением ПЗУ его необходимо отключить. Просто перережьте дорожку на линии ROMCS на краевом разъеме. Но зачем его вообще извлекать? Чтобы использовать другое ПО, вы просто выходите из программы. Если вы используете +2, то POKE 23611,23 в любом случае переведет вас в режим 128K с подключенным модемом.

Хотя в прошивке ПЗУ VTX и НАПИСАНО, что это терминал Micronet, это лишь потому, что деньги Micronet пошли на его оплату. Он прекрасно способен подключаться к любой британской системе Viewdata. Я без проблем использовал его на TAS, TAO, TSV и Speedlink. Вот несколько советов.

Чтобы использовать его в системе, где вы не знаете требований к авторизации, зайдите в главное меню, нажмите BREAK, затем RUN. Это позволит перейти прямо в режим терминала без искажения символов. Затем вы просто выходите на связь и переходите в режим терминала вместо использования пункта log on.

Если связь обрывается во время входа в систему, попробуйте выйти на линию во время более позднего тонального сигнала. Это связано с тем, что многие модемы сканируют скорости передачи данных, которые вообще не использовались, когда разрабатывался VTX, поэтому он не слышит тоны и сбрасывает линию.

Для большинства BBS в мире сейчас требуются программы с поддержкой прокрутки (scrolling software). На моей кассете PD Tape 1 кое-что из этого есть [см. OUTBOARD], и всего за £1... Я, должно быть, сошел с ума! Также учтите, что на некоторых досках используются модемы американского производства, которые вообще не поддерживают V23, поэтому подключиться к ним не удастся.

* «f» = выбор графической последовательности.
* «d» = то же самое.
* «r» = скорость движения изображения.
* «x» = скорость смены направления.
* «z» = скорость смены цветов.
* «n» = скорость движения по горизонтали.
* «m» = скорость движения по вертикали.
* «s» = горизонтальная симметрия (9 — симметрия относительно центра).
* «a» = вертикальная симметрия.
* «u» = выбор типа узора.
* «c» = длина шлейфа (эффективная плотность узора).
* «i» = цвет изображения (ink); (0–7 задают фиксированный цвет; 8–9 = меняющийся).
